correctness.rationale: For each deleted pair, no third vertex can strongly resolve its endpoints because their mutual distance is 3 while every third vertex has distance profile {1,2}; hence every strong resolving set hits every pair. If all pairs are hit, a selected matched mate strongly resolves any two omitted vertices because the second omitted vertex lies on a length-3 geodesic across that matched pair. A hitting set is non-dominating precisely when some omitted a_i has S intersect B equal to {b_i}, or symmetrically, forcing exactly the 2n exceptional transversals. The three choices per pair give z^n(z+2)^n before those exceptions are removed. Exhaustive direct checks over n=3..8 independently confirm membership and coefficients.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a standard canonical bipartite/direct-product family, and strong resolving domination intentionally couples two established structural requirements. The final result is a complete all-set classification: it identifies exactly 2n obstructions among an exponentially large family of strong resolving sets, determines every cardinality count, and classifies every optimum. This is more informative than the already-known strong metric scalar and provides a reusable structural description of when domination adds a genuine constraint.
